audit_findings.title: Acquisition-funded growth may be treated as costless organic growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $275.5 million of acquisition cash outflow in 2024 and $41.6 million in 2025; the 2024 amount equals 15.9% of the $1,737.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired operations enter historical OE and the growth evidence, while acquisition payments remain outside recurring OE and no acquisition perimeter or organic-growth decomposition is supplied.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 1, 2024 ( “Lacework Acquisition Date ”), we acquired Lacework Inc. (“Lacework”), a privately held data-driven cloud security company, for $ 152.3 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisitions and cash payments are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much forecast growth depends on repeating them. The 2024 cash outflow alone is large relative to anchor OE, and reducing both distributable cash and the 8%-10% growth premise could materially alter the scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic from acquired revenue and OE for 2024-2026, identify acquisition payments required to sustain forecast growth, and rerun all scenarios with either organic growth rates or a recurring acquisition-reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized sales commissions may leave a recurring cash cost outside the earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $112.7 million net 2025 investment, computed as $449.0 million additions less $336.3 million amortization; 6.5% of anchor OE and approximately $2.78 per base-case share if wholly omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted increase in deferred contract costs would overstate anchor OE because cash commissions paid exceed the amortization included in accounting earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognize sales commissions expenses related to product sales upfront while sales commissions expenses for service contracts are deferred as deferred contract costs in the consolidated balance sheets and amortized over the applicable amortization period.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether an error exists remains unresolved because the OE reconciliation is absent; an operating-cash-flow-based calculation would already capture the net investment. Even assuming the entire $112.7 million was omitted, the computed base-case effect is about $2.78 per share, versus a $48.33 base value and $156.36 market price, so it would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $449.0 million deferred-contract-cost cash outflow and $336.3 million amortization through the 2025 OE reconciliation; correct the anchor only if the net $112.7 million was not captured.

audit_findings.title: The growth cases may not incorporate disclosed near-term margin compression
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 operating margin was 32.6%, up 3.8 percentage points from 28.8%, while revenue rose 23% and operating income rose 39%
audit_findings.mechanism: Margin compression would reduce forecast OE growth through higher personnel, cloud, data-center and real-estate costs relative to revenue.
audit_findings.evidence: Total revenue is expected to increase in 2026 compared to the prior year; however, our expenses are expected to outpace revenue growth, primarily reflecting investments in sales and marketing headcount, product development and the continued capital expenditures in data centers and real estate.
audit_findings.explanation: The original warning was forward-looking and has not appeared in the latest filed results: first-half operating leverage improved, and management now expects full-year 2026 operating margin to increase slightly rather than decline. Higher component, data-center and investment costs remain prospective risks, not a demonstrated omission in current numbers.
audit_findings.action: Monitor full-year 2026 OE, gross margins, operating margin and capital expenditures; rerun growth cases if actual normalized OE growth falls below the modeled 8%-10% range.

audit_findings.title: Non-operating acquisition gains could contaminate the anchor and historical trend
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.9 million in 2025 and $106.3 million in 2024; the 2025 amount is 2.3% of anchor OE and approximately $0.99 per base-case share if wholly included
audit_findings.mechanism: Bargain-purchase and remeasurement gains could improperly increase OE; the 2024 gain could also inflate the historical trend, although the model anchors to the lower 2025 actual.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded a gain on bargain purchase of $39.9 million related to our acquisition of Linksys during the first quarter of 2025 as compared to a gain on bargain purchase of $106.3 million related to our acquisition of Lacework recorded during the third quarter of 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Removal is not demonstrated by the supplied OE reconciliation, so contamination remains possible. Its valuation scale is bounded: fully removing the $39.9 million 2025 bargain-purchase gain would reduce base value by about $0.99 per share. The $106.3 million 2024 gain cannot raise the selected anchor because the trend estimate was already capped at the lower 2025 actual. Neither changes the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document the OE adjustments for the $39.9 million and $106.3 million bargain-purchase gains and the $10.8 million 2025 Linksys remeasurement gain; rerun only for any amount actually retained.

audit_findings.title: Potentially uncapped indemnification claims are an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured payment would reduce cash or future OE before value reaches common equity and may require a bridge deduction if a presently estimable claim exists.
audit_findings.evidence: However, certain agreements include covenants, penalties and indemnification provisions including and beyond indemnification for third-party claims of IP infringement that could potentially expose us to losses in excess of the amount received under the agreement, and in some instances to potential liability that is not contractually limited.
audit_findings.explanation: Pending indemnification claims are demonstrated, but the latest filing reports no material awards to date, immaterial litigation accruals and no estimable loss range. Because some exposure is uncapped, the record cannot bound the downside or establish whether it is material; this is an unresolved contingent claim rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain claim-level amounts, contractual caps, defense costs, insurance limits and exclusions, counsel's probability assessment, and any reasonably possible loss range; deduct or scenario-test any supported exposure.

audit_findings.title: A 2025 tax-timing benefit may inflate cash-based owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $120.0 million, equal to 6.9% of anchor OE and approximately $2.96 per base-case share if fully nonrecurring and wholly included
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary reduction in cash taxes could inflate the 2025 OE anchor if cash taxes were used without normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the Act, our income tax liability in 2025 decreased by $120.0 million and our GAAP effective tax rate for 2025 increased by one percentage point.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $120.0 million reduction in 2025 tax liability, but not that the entire amount was a one-time cash benefit embedded in OE; the legislation is permanent and the filing also says the GAAP effective tax rate increased. Even under the conservative assumption that all $120.0 million should be removed, base value falls by about $2.96 per share from $48.33, which does not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $156.36 price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile tax provision, cash taxes paid, deferred taxes and the Act-related liability reduction to OE; normalize only the portion shown to be a nonrecurring timing benefit.
